extracted.intended_audience: educators, college administrators, school policymakers, and informed general readers interested in education reform
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial discussion of principles for college and school governance and curricular aims, arguing for student self-government, scientific modes of instruction to combat credulity, and cautioning against comprehensive state control of education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student self-government in colleges
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be permitted 'perfect freedom in the election of courses of study' and treated as responsible agents rather than subjected to espionage or intrusive surveillance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement broad student freedom in course selection; discard systems of espionage; view students as 'self-respecting, responsible, and possessed of enough common-sense'; reduce reliance on recitation-marks; treat failure in final examinations as primarily the student's loss rather than grounds for punitive publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private corrective discipline rather than public punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: When students abuse freedom or disturb order, faculty should use private admonition or quietly advise a student to leave rather than public shaming or publicity of expulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer private admonition from a chairman or faculty member; use advice to leave as a discreet remedy; avoid public expulsions and other publicity that stigmatize students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-run judicial processes (students' courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local or student courts can adjudicate student matters without necessarily creating conflict with faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where adopted (e.g., students' court), ensure clear rules and cooperation with faculty; use these bodies sparingly and in ways that avoid escalating tensions with administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend appropriate measures of self-government into schools
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'large measure of self-government is quite admissible' even for pupils below college age; experiments (school republics with officers subject to the same laws) have been instructive and largely successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt elements of republican self-government (elective student officers, shared rules) to lower school grades, with safeguards to ensure age-appropriate responsibility and oversight by teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachers must adapt to social evolution and respect student freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should respect 'freedom of thought, of belief, of action' that modern civilization requires, and adjust methods accordingly; failure to do so indicates the teacher should seek other fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid autocratic classroom control and corporal punishment (e.g., 'the birch rod'); encourage autonomy, free inquiry, and respect for individual rights in classroom practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate habit of doubt and evidence-based judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Credulity is corrected by 'doubt, distrust, an appreciation of the importance of evidence, and a trained capacity to judge of it'; disbelief as an attitude should be encouraged until evidence proves valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students habits of critical inquiry: demand evidence, weigh testimony, and develop a disposition to question improbable claims; integrate exercises that require evaluation of evidence in practical contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific education as the principal remedy for credulity
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in the 'methods of scientific study' is the 'only adequate remedy' for lax thinking and popular credulity; scientific education naturally fosters the spirit of doubt necessary to resist impostures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize scientific method across curriculum—hypothesis, testing, reliance on empirical evidence—not merely factual memorization; prioritize laboratory/field work and reasoning over purely verbal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary education alone is inadequate for practical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary culture 'neither prepares the mind to deal intelligently with questions of evidence nor does it imbue it with right conceptions of social order' and may impede the study of things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid curricula dominated exclusively by verbal/critical literary study; balance literature with science and practical studies that develop analytic skills and understanding of social causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach social laws and cause-effect relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should 'familiarize the mind with the conception of an order in human life, the invincible operation of cause and effect in social affairs, and the laws of proportion between actions and consequences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instruction that emphasizes social causation and consequences (not as rote theory) so students understand predictable relations in social/economic life; use case studies and empirical social inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political economy/social science must be taught as method, not rote
rubrics_metrics.description: While instruction in political economy would be useful, merely adding social science as another subject taught 'in the manner of other studies' will not solve credulity; it must be taught scientifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If introducing economics or social science, teach them with experimental, empirical, and methodological rigor rather than as descriptive, memorized content; avoid superficial or purely literary treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form educational aims to promote self-reliance and industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should encourage dependence on 'one's own efforts' and virtues of 'industry, frugality, and self-denial' rather than nurturing expectation of government largess or easy providence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape curricula and civic instruction to valorize productive habits, personal responsibility, and prudent planning rather than cultivating expectations of charity or political patronage as normal economic strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against comprehensive state control of education
rubrics_metrics.description: State control and compulsory, comprehensive state education risk lowering standards: 'education by authority and political machinery must fall to a lower standard than that which has been attained by former methods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor diverse, voluntary, and private initiatives in education; resist centralization that substitutes political machinery for local, voluntary, or private educational enterprise; scrutinize proposals that would make the state the sole organizer of all grades of schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect individual rights against extension of state sovereignty into education
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that the state has 'the right of the custody and control of the citizen... as complete as the right of the parent' is criticized as dissolving individual rights and incompatible with progress toward liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame educational policy so that parental and individual rights are preserved; avoid legal doctrines or administrative practices that treat citizens as wholly subject to state custody in educational matters.
